landing.title: Thai Massage
landing.description: What is Thai massage, and what actually happens in a session? Here's a plain-English guide to the technique, the history and what to expect.

content.imageAlt: Therapist guiding a client through an assisted stretch during a Thai massage
content.h2: Part stretch, part acupressure, entirely clothed
content.paragraph1: Thai massage is one of the oldest forms of bodywork still practised today — a mix of rhythmic pressure and gentle, yoga-like stretching that follows the body's energy lines, known as Sen. Unlike an oil massage, it's done fully clothed on a padded mat or firm treatment table, with no oils or lotions involved.
content.paragraph2: Your therapist uses their hands, thumbs, forearms and sometimes feet to apply steady pressure along the Sen lines, easing you into stretches you'd recognise from a yoga class — except someone else is doing the work. It sounds like hard graft on paper. In practice, most people find it deeply relaxing, and it's worth trying if lying still under oil has never quite done it for you.
content.h3_2: What to expect from your session
content.orderedList1: Wear something loose and comfortable — you'll be moving, not just lying still.
content.orderedList2: Your therapist works methodically from feet to head along the Sen lines, combining pressure with assisted stretches.
content.orderedList3: Sessions usually run 60–90 minutes, and it's completely normal to feel looser for days afterwards.
content.unorderedList1: Eases stiff joints and improves flexibility — especially handy if you spend all day at a desk.
content.unorderedList2: Releases muscular tension without oil, so there's no need to shower straight after.
content.unorderedList3: Combines massage and stretching in one session, so you leave both looser and calmer.
